summary:
HELIOS (Human Exploration Life Intelligence & Observation System) is a prototype astronaut health monitoring and mission-support platform designed for long-duration human spaceflight. It provides a centralized interface for monitoring crew health, reviewing biometric telemetry, conducting daily crew check-ins, assessing cognitive performance, tracking potential health risks, monitoring environmental conditions, and supporting communication between astronauts and ground control.
Built using React, TypeScript, FastAPI, Python, and SQLite, HELIOS combines simulated astronaut telemetry with health-monitoring and mission-management tools. Its design considers NASA's Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and hostile or closed environments.
HELIOS aims to help mission teams organize health information, identify potential concerns, and maintain crew awareness when communication with Earth may be delayed. It demonstrates how an integrated digital health-monitoring system could support safer and more informed decisions during future missions to the Moon and Mars.
details:
HELIOS is a web-based astronaut health monitoring and mission-support prototype developed to address the challenges of maintaining crew health during long-duration space missions.

The platform provides a centralized mission dashboard with several integrated modules:

• Mission Overview: Presents an overview of the simulated mission and crew status.

• Crew Health Monitoring: Displays astronaut biometric measurements and telemetry, including heart rate, oxygen saturation, body temperature, blood pressure, and other health-related parameters.

• Crew Assessment: Supports daily crew check-ins and cognitive assessment activities, including a reaction-time test.

• Telemetry Monitoring: Organizes incoming measurements and provides historical telemetry information for observation.

• Risk Monitor: Includes a risk assessment system that evaluates incoming measurements against defined plausibility ranges and supports the identification of potential concerns.

• Environment Monitoring: Provides a dedicated interface for mission-environment information.

• Ground Control: Provides a communication interface designed around the operational challenges of communicating with Earth during space missions, including delayed or queued messages.

The backend is developed using Python and FastAPI, with SQLAlchemy and SQLite for data management. The frontend uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Recharts, and Lucide React.

HELIOS uses simulated astronaut profiles and synthetic telemetry to demonstrate the system's functionality. The prototype is designed around NASA's Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight, providing a mission-oriented framework for considering physical health, cognitive performance, environmental conditions, and communication limitations.

The intended impact is to demonstrate how health information and mission-support functions can be brought together in one interface, helping crews and mission teams maintain situational awareness during exploration missions where immediate assistance from Earth may not always be available.

HELIOS is an experimental prototype. Its simulated data and risk assessments are not clinically validated and must not be used for real medical diagnosis or treatment.
